subject: Proposal: Short extension + usage buffer for Nexus POC
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@nexus.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Short extension + usage buffer for Nexus POC

Hi Samir,

Thanks again for the time today — quick follow up with a compact proposal that should keep your evaluation momentum while staying within the constraints you mentioned. High level: a short, time-boxed extension plus a small credited usage buffer to cover peak runs.

Proposal (flex option):
- Extension: +10 calendar days to current POC end date
- Usage buffer: 30 GPU-hours credited to Nexus account (applied to the POC billing)
- Commercial sweetener: one-time 7% credit applied on the first invoice after conversion to a paid plan (or applied as a credit if you convert to reserved capacity within 30 days)

We can formalize this as a short amendment (signed) and push the buffer immediately so your engineers can continue benchmark runs. If this looks sensible I can kick off the amendment and provide a DocuSign link — otherwise tell me where we should move the numbers (length, hours, discount) and I’ll route to pricing/finance.

Attaching a quick usage buffer calc (estimated) to show how 30 hours maps to your throughput runs.

Thanks,
Irene

Subject: Re: Proposal: Short extension + usage buffer for Nexus POC

Irene — appreciate the quick proposal. We’re close, but three asks from our side before we can sign: 

1) Can we get a 14-day extension instead of 10? Our infra team is running a second sweep of tests and the additional days are easier than re-scheduling.
2) Can the buffer be 40 GPU-hours? We have a heavy tail in some inference jobs and want to be confident the trial covers that.
3) Commercially — our finance prefers a simple % discount rather than a conditional credit. Would Redwood consider a 10% one-time discount applied to the pilot invoice?

Also, procurement will need the amendment and a PO. Legal will want to see the amendment language (standard terms are OK). If you can send a redline-friendly term sheet we’ll loop legal.

If we can get close on these items this week, we’ll execute quickly.

Thanks — Samir

Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Nexus asks (14d ext / 40h buffer / 10% discount) — quick pricing input needed

Folks — looping you in for a fast decision. Nexus pushed back with a slightly longer extension and a higher buffer (14 days / 40 GPU-hours) and asks for a 10% one-time discount instead of the conditional credit.

My read: we can compromise and protect margin by doing a time-limited credit + smaller buffer. Suggested counter: 10 days extension, 30 hours buffer, 7% one-time credit OR 5% simple discount (team preference?) — and require signed amendment + PO. Also propose adding one week of dedicated onboarding support (no charge) as a low-cost value add.

Please reply with: approve as-is, or change numbers. Finance/legal review required if we move discount >7%. Need decision today to keep momentum.

Irene / team — quick guardrails from Sales Ops / Finance:

- We can approve an extension up to 10 days without escalating. 14 days is a bit long from a capacity planning perspective.
- Buffer: approve 30 GPU-hours credited to the trial. 40 is outside the usual concession band for this stage.
- Discount: we should avoid a recurring or structural % discount on list price. Offer a one-time credit of 7% on the first invoice (applied as an invoice credit) — that preserves ARR math and is easier for revenue ops.

Operational asks: require a signed amendment + PO before credits are applied. If legal needs to redline, route to Contracts (I’ll introduce Chris).

I’ve attached a short term-sheet we can use as the amendment template.

If Irene needs any concession tweaks (e.g., 10 days -> 9) let me know; otherwise greenlight on 10d / 30h / 7% credit.
